name: SunSpec Alliance
summary: Information models, IEEE 2030.5 / CSIP certification and interoperability programs for distributed energy resources.
description: SunSpec Alliance publishes the SunSpec Modbus information models that solar inverters, batteries and meters expose, and runs certification programs for them and for IEEE 2030.5 / CSIP, for products used with California's investor-owned utilities under Rule 21.

standards.name: SunSpec Modbus and the SunSpec information models
IEEE 2030.5 / CSIP
standards.note: Publishes the CSIP conformance test procedures; testing runs at Authorized Test Labs.

specifications.detail: "All SunSpec specifications are free to download and use." Most downloads ask for a name, company and email.

community.detail: Webinars and specifications are open; working-group participation starts with Individual membership.

organizationFree.detail: Company participation starts with Contributing membership at $5,000 a year.

workingGroups.detail: The membership table marks working groups as not included for non-members.

interopTesting.detail: Certification testing runs at Authorized Test Labs, which set their own fees; non-members can certify.

certification.detail: Non-members can certify at a $10,000 certification fee; Contributing members pay $5,000.

openSource.detail: The SunSpec Modbus model definitions are published on GitHub; the reference implementation needs membership.

memberships.name: Non-member
memberships.note: Free specifications and certification registry; certification fee $10,000.

memberships.name: Individual
memberships.eligibility: Academics, individual researchers, hobbyists, open-source developers and other individuals.
memberships.note: Personal participation; certification fee $10,000.

memberships.name: Contributing
memberships.note: Unlimited company participation; certification fee $5,000 plus certification and software discounts.

programs.name: SunSpec IEEE 2030.5 / CSIP certification
programs.detail: Certifies IEEE 2030.5 clients, gateways, aggregators and servers for California Rule 21. Testing at an Authorized Test Lab; SunSpec evaluates the results against CSIP and its test procedures.

related.relation: IEEE SA publishes IEEE 2030.5; SunSpec certifies products against the CSIP profile of it.
SunSpec Modbus runs on the Modbus protocol that the Modbus Organization maintains.

insights: SunSpec is a good example of why "open" needs splitting up. The specifications are free to download and use, working groups are for members, and certification is open to anyone but costs twice as much without a Contributing membership.

The Individual tier is aimed at academics, researchers, hobbyists and open-source developers. At $1,000 a year it is a real cost for a lone maintainer, but it is the route into working groups for someone who does not represent a company.

For IEEE 2030.5, SunSpec is the certification body for California's CSIP profile, not the publisher of the standard: IEEE SA publishes IEEE 2030.5 itself. The certification test procedures are free to download from the specifications page, which makes them a useful public reference for independent implementations.

name: Modbus Organization

certification.detail: General members get discounts on conformance testing; the page does not say whether non-members can test.

memberships.name: Supporting
memberships.eligibility: Companies providing system integration services with Modbus.

programs.name: Conformance Self-Test Program

name: OPC Foundation
summary: Develops OPC UA, runs certification test labs and maintains the open-source .NET reference stack.
description: The OPC Foundation develops and maintains the OPC UA specifications, publishes them openly, runs accredited certification test labs and compliance test tools, and maintains the UA-.NETStandard reference implementation on GitHub.

specifications.detail: The benefits table gives non-members access to the OPC UA specifications. OPC Classic specifications are for members.

community.detail: Specifications and the open-source stack are public; working groups need a paid membership.

individualFree.detail: Membership is for organizations; there is no individual category.

organizationFree.detail: The UA Logo membership is $0 for companies that offer OPC UA products. It gives certification access but no voting and no working groups.

workingGroups.detail: Working groups are open to Corporate, Startup, End-User and Non-Voting members, not to UA Logo members or non-members.

interopTesting.detail: Interoperability workshops are listed on the certification pages; we found no published eligibility.

certification.detail: Certification is "a premium service available to OPC Foundation members and logo members", so it needs at least the free UA Logo membership.

openSource.detail: Maintains the UA-.NETStandard reference stack on GitHub.

memberships.name: UA Logo
memberships.eligibility: Companies that offer OPC UA products.
memberships.note: Certification lab access at the logo-member rate; test tools as a service.

memberships.name: Startup
memberships.eligibility: First five years and revenue under $2M.
memberships.note: Compliance test tools and certification lab access included.

memberships.name: Non-Voting
memberships.eligibility: Government, research, universities and non-profits that do not build or market OPC products.

memberships.name: End-User
memberships.eligibility: Organizations that use OPC-based products.

memberships.name: Corporate, classes D to A
memberships.eligibility: By annual sales: Class D under $2M ($3,000), C $2M to $20M ($4,800), B $20M to $100M ($9,600), A $100M to $1B ($18,000).
memberships.note: Free compliance test tools; 50% discount at the certification lab.

memberships.name: Corporate, classes AA and AAA
memberships.eligibility: Sales over $1B.
memberships.note: The dues table shows two 2027 figures per class without saying which applies, so we do not repeat them here.

programs.name: OPC UA certification
programs.detail: Testing at an OPC Foundation accredited Certification Test Lab: €900 per day for Corporate members, €1,800 per day for logo members. A server usually takes 3 to 7 days, a client 5 to 10.

programs.name: Compliance Test Tool (CTT)
programs.detail: Free for Corporate and Startup members; offered as a service to End-User, Non-Voting and UA Logo members.

related.relation: Hosts Eclipse Milo, an independent open-source OPC UA stack.

insights: OPC UA is one of the few industrial standards where a non-member can read the current specifications without paying, and where the standards body itself maintains an open-source reference stack. That combination makes independent implementations practical.

The membership ladder is unusually fine-grained. A company with an OPC UA product can join as a UA Logo member for $0 and certify, a young company can vote and join working groups as a Startup for $500, and research bodies and non-profits get working-group access as Non-Voting members for $900.

Certification is not open to non-members, but the lowest route to it is the free logo membership. The day rate at the test lab is twice as high for logo members as for Corporate members, so the cheapest route on paper is not always the cheapest in practice.

name: BACnet International
summary: Promotes BACnet and runs BTL testing, certification and the PlugFest; free individual participation.

workingGroups.detail: The individual page does not mention committees or working groups.

certification.detail: BTL certification does not require membership. Non-members pay an annual listing fee of $2,500 per product; corporate members in good standing are exempt.

memberships.eligibility: Manufacturers and OEMs of BACnet software, hardware or related services.

memberships.eligibility: Manufacturers and OEMs that support BACnet Interest Groups outside the United States.

programs.name: BTL certification
programs.detail: Testing at a Recognized BACnet Testing Organization, then a free application and an annual listing fee of $2,500 per product for non-members.

programs.name: BTL PlugFest
programs.detail: Interoperability workshop for developers; corporate members get registration discounts.

name: ASHRAE
summary: Publishes ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135 (BACnet) through its BACnet Committee, SSPC 135.
description: ASHRAE is the professional society that publishes the BACnet standard, ANSI/ASHRAE 135. Its BACnet Committee (SSPC 135) develops and maintains the standard, with working groups that recruit volunteers.

specifications.detail: 135-2024 is available as a free, read-only PDF; downloadable copies and other editions are sold through the ASHRAE and ISO stores.

name: International Electrotechnical Commission
summary: Publishes IEC 61850 and IEC 60870-5 through TC 57, and the IEC 61158 and 61784 fieldbus series through SC 65C; experts join via national committees.
description: The IEC is the international standards organization for electrical and electronic technologies. Its Technical Committee 57 (power systems management and associated information exchange) maintains the IEC 61850 substation automation series and the IEC 60870-5 telecontrol protocols, including IEC 60870-5-104. Subcommittee 65C (industrial networks) maintains the IEC 61158 fieldbus and IEC 61784 profile series, in which the CIP networks, EtherNet/IP among them, are Communication Profile Family 2 and PROFINET and PROFIBUS are Communication Profile Family 3.

standards.name: IEC 61850 (TC 57 WG 10, power system IED communication)
IEC 61158 and IEC 61784 industrial networks, including CPF 2 for the CIP networks and CPF 3 for PROFINET and PROFIBUS (SC 65C)

specifications.detail: Standards are sold through the IEC webstore. The complete IEC 61850 series pack lists at CHF 26,508.

organizationFree.detail: Members of the IEC are national committees, not companies.

workingGroups.detail: "Each NC (National Committee) can appoint experts to take part in specific technical work." Conditions and costs depend on the national committee.

interopTesting.detail: TC 57 writes standards; IEC 61850 interoperability testing is organized by UCAIug.

memberships.eligibility: Experts nominated by the national committee of their country of residence, such as the Standards Council of Canada's mirror committee for TC 57.

The 62443 security series is published jointly as ISA/IEC 62443.
ODVA maintains CIP and EtherNet/IP; IEC 61784-1-2 profiles them as CPF 2.
PI maintains PROFINET and PROFIBUS; IEC 61784-2 profiles them as CPF 3.

name: UCA International Users Group
summary: User groups for IEC 61850, CIM and OpenFMB, and the IEC 61850 interoperability (IOP) testing event.
description: The UCA International Users Group is a community of utilities, vendors and labs around utility communication standards. It hosts the 61850, CIM and OpenFMB user groups and organizes IEC 61850 interoperability testing.

memberships.eligibility: By annual revenue: tier 1 under $1M is $1,375 (5 accounts), tier 2 $1M to $10M is $2,750, up to tier 8 over $100B at $20,000.
memberships.note: Corporate members vote for the Board of Directors.

memberships.name: Sustaining
memberships.eligibility: Unlimited accounts.

memberships.name: Individual Consultant

memberships.name: University
memberships.eligibility: Students, educators and researchers; one account.

memberships.name: Public utility commission
memberships.eligibility: Public utility commissions; one account.

programs.name: IEC 61850 Interoperability Testing (IOP)
programs.detail: Multi-day interoperability event for vendors, utilities, labs, integrators and standards organizations. The 2024 edition ran 12 to 20 September in Birmingham, Alabama.

related.relation: IEC TC 57 develops IEC 61850 and CIM; UCAIug supports their users and tests interoperability.
LF Energy hosts open-source IEC 61850 tooling such as CoMPAS.

insights: For IEC 61850, the committee that writes the standard and the community that tests it are different bodies. IEC TC 57 develops the standard, and experts reach it through national committees. UCAIug is where utilities, vendors and labs meet to share experience and run the interoperability (IOP) events.

Corporate membership is priced by revenue and starts at $1,375 a year for companies under $1M. Individual, university and regulator memberships exist but are priced on request, so a solo engineer has to ask.

The IOP is the main public venue where independent IEC 61850 implementations meet. Its page invites global stakeholders without stating a membership requirement, so it is worth asking the organizers directly before planning around it.

name: DNP Users Group

description: The DNP Users Group supports the DNP3 protocol, standardized as IEEE 1815. It keeps the member-only technical document library, runs workshops, and offers conformance testing services at member and non-member rates.

organizationFree.detail: Commercial members start with Micro vendor at $500.

workingGroups.detail: The fee guide does not list technical committee access per category.

interopTesting.detail: We found no public interoperability event.

certification.detail: Non-members can buy conformance test access at $15,000 per project; members get 0 to 100% discounts on the $1,200 (P1) and $2,400 (P2) per-interface services.

openSource.detail: We found no open-source project maintained by the group.

memberships.name: Emeritus

name: IEEE Standards Association
summary: Publishes IEEE 1815 (DNP3) and IEEE 2030.5; working-group participation is open to everyone.
description: The IEEE Standards Association develops IEEE standards, including IEEE 1815 (DNP3) and IEEE 2030.5 (Smart Energy Profile 2.0). Individual-based standards development is open to anyone; membership adds balloting and leadership rights.

standards.name: IEEE 1815 (DNP3), revision P1815 in progress
standards.note: Power System Communications and Cybersecurity committee, Power and Energy Society.

workingGroups.detail: Individual-based working groups are open to everyone; membership is needed to lead groups.

Certifies IEEE 2030.5 products against the CSIP profile.

name: ODVA
summary: Maintains CIP and EtherNet/IP, licenses vendors, runs conformance testing and hosts the PlugFest interoperability events.
description: ODVA, founded in 1995 as the Open DeviceNet Vendors Association, maintains the Common Industrial Protocol and its network adaptations EtherNet/IP, DeviceNet, ControlNet and CompoNet. It sells the specifications by subscription, assigns vendor IDs to licensed vendors, issues a Declaration of Conformity after conformance testing at its test service providers, and runs PlugFest interoperability events.

standards.name: The CIP Networks Library: CIP, EtherNet/IP, CIP Security and the other volumes
Conformance testing and the Declaration of Conformity

specifications.detail: The specifications are sold as annual subscriptions, updated twice a year, and need signed Terms of Usage first. Prices are on the order form only.

community.detail: PlugFest events are open without membership; Special Interest Groups are listed as a member benefit.

individualFree.detail: Membership is limited to Licensed Vendors of ODVA technologies, which are companies.

organizationFree.detail: Membership levels and fees are not published on the pages we checked; the order form only lists member discounts.

workingGroups.detail: Joining Special Interest Groups is listed as a member benefit; we found no statement on access for non-members.

interopTesting.detail: The PlugFest page states that ODVA membership is not required.

certification.detail: Conformance testing needs no membership, but the vendor must be a Licensed Vendor, with signed Terms of Usage, a vendor ID, a specification subscription and a conformance test software subscription.

openSource.detail: The developer hub offers ODVACompress source code after registration; we found no open-source protocol stack maintained by ODVA. OpENer is maintained by the independent EIP Stack Group.

memberships.name: Licensed Vendor
memberships.eligibility: A company that signs the ODVA Application and Agreement for Membership and Terms of Usage, the technology licence; needed before buying specifications or a vendor ID.
memberships.note: Pays the non-member price for specifications, vendor IDs and test software.

memberships.name: Associate member
memberships.eligibility: Licensed Vendors that can show intent to make and sell products using ODVA technologies.
memberships.note: 25% discount on specifications, vendor IDs and conformance test software.

memberships.name: Regular or Principal member
memberships.eligibility: Licensed Vendors.
memberships.note: 50% discount on specifications, vendor IDs and conformance test software.

programs.name: ODVA conformance testing
programs.detail: Every product with ODVA technology must pass vendor-independent conformance testing, which results in a Declaration of Conformity. Test service providers: ODVA in Ann Arbor (USA), TÜV Rheinland in Yokohama (Japan) and Taicang (China), and Otto-von-Guericke-Universität Magdeburg (Germany). Fees are not published.

programs.name: ODVA conformance test software
programs.detail: A subscription that vendors must buy before conformance test services; members get 25% or 50% off.

programs.name: EtherNet/IP PlugFest
programs.detail: A three-day event where vendors exercise their products against other vendors' in a live system, using ODVA's interoperability test procedures (Pub 95).

documents.label: Request the Application and Agreement for Membership and Terms of Usage
The Common Industrial Protocol and the Family of CIP Networks (PUB00123)

related.relation: IEC 61158 and IEC 61784-1-2 include the CIP networks as Communication Profile Family 2, with EtherNet/IP as profile CP 2/2.

sources.label: Getting started: specifications, vendor ID and Terms of Usage
Specification, vendor ID and test software order form

insights: Building EtherNet/IP into a product is a licensing relationship before it is a membership question: Terms of Usage, a vendor ID, a specification subscription and a conformance test are needed whether or not a company joins.

Open-source implementers work without the specifications. OpENer was first released by Rockwell Automation, and newer stacks such as go-ethernetip are built from public documents and the behaviour of other implementations. That keeps the code open, but leaves conformance to the companies that ship products on it.
The PlugFest is the cheapest way in for a young company: it needs no membership and tests a product against other vendors' devices in a live system, well before the formal conformance test.
ODVA does not publish its fees on its website, so comparing the cost of entry with the OPC Foundation or the DNP Users Group needs a quote.

name: PROFIBUS & PROFINET International
summary: Maintains PROFINET, PROFIBUS and IO-Link, runs mandatory PROFINET certification through PI Test Labs and offers members its Community Stack.
description: PROFIBUS & PROFINET International is the umbrella of the PROFIBUS Nutzerorganisation (PNO) in Germany and the Regional PI Associations around the world. It maintains the PROFINET and PROFIBUS specifications and profiles such as PROFIsafe, PROFIdrive and PROFIenergy, and IO-Link. Certification by an independent PI Test Lab is mandatory for every PROFINET device, members get the specifications, the PROFINET Test Bundle and the PROFINET Community Stack, and regional associations hold Plugfests. The protocols are also in IEC 61158 and IEC 61784 as Communication Profile Family 3.

standards.name: PROFINET and PROFIBUS specifications, with the PROFIsafe, PROFIdrive and PROFIenergy profiles, and GSDML
PROFINET certification through PI Test Labs and the PI Certification Office
PROFINET Community Stack, for members
standards.note: Source code for members under the PNO Community Source Code License, not an open-source licence.

specifications.detail: Access to the specifications is listed as a member benefit for device manufacturers. The IEC 61158 and 61784 versions are sold by the IEC.

community.detail: Membership runs through a Regional PI Association; member-only training documents and webinars are listed as benefits, while public guides and the PI forum are open.

individualFree.detail: The membership pages describe device manufacturers, users and consultants, and a separate student membership; we found no free individual tier.

organizationFree.detail: Fees are not on the membership pages; applicants are sent to their Regional PI Association.

workingGroups.detail: Companies that join working groups must accept the TC/WG guidelines, the codes of conduct and the IPR policy; we found no statement on access for non-members.

interopTesting.detail: Regional associations hold Plugfests, such as PI North America's in April 2026 with thirteen companies; the page does not say whether membership is required.

certification.detail: Certification is mandatory for PROFINET and open to non-members, but the certificate costs EUR 6,000 instead of EUR 1,800, the PROFINET Test Bundle is for members only, non-members must license the patents themselves and may not use the PROFINET logo.

openSource.detail: The PROFINET Community Stack is free of charge for members only, under the PNO Community Source Code License, which forbids combining it with copyleft code.

memberships.name: Member, through a Regional PI Association
memberships.eligibility: Companies and research institutions; device manufacturers and users and consultants have different benefit sets.
memberships.note: Specifications, patent rights, test tools, the Community Stack and certification discounts.

programs.name: PROFINET certification
programs.detail: A test at an independent PI Test Lab, paid to the lab, then a certificate from the PI Certification Office: EUR 1,800 for members, EUR 6,000 for non-members. Valid for three years; any change to the device invalidates it. Device certificates for products, technology certificates for stacks, ASICs and evaluation boards.

programs.name: PROFINET Test Bundle
programs.detail: The test software of the certification test, downloadable free of charge by members; non-members have no access.

programs.name: PROFINET Plugfest
programs.detail: Vendors test controllers and devices against each other, often before certification. PI North America's fourth was held in April 2026 with seven controllers and fifteen devices.

related.relation: IEC 61158 and IEC 61784-2 include PROFINET and PROFIBUS as Communication Profile Family 3.

insights: PROFINET is the one protocol in this directory where certification is mandatory for every device, and it is open to non-members at a higher fee. The test software is not, so a young company in practice joins before it certifies.

PI's own source code, the Community Stack, is free but members-only and cannot be combined with copyleft code. Open implementers therefore work from public documents, Wireshark's dissectors and each other's behaviour, as go-profinet does with p-net, pnio-rs and profinet-py.
OT Fabric is not a PI member. go-profinet lists what that costs, from official schema validation to certification, in its PI-MEMBERSHIP document, and makes no conformance claim.

name: CAN in Automation
summary: Nonprofit association of CAN users and manufacturers: CAN FD and CAN XL recommendations, CANopen and device profiles, conformance testing and plugfests.
description: CAN in Automation was founded in March 1992 as a nonprofit association of users and manufacturers, with its office in Nuremberg, Germany, and lists 749 members. Its members develop and publish CiA specifications: CAN FD and CAN XL specifications and recommendations, CAN FD Light, CANopen and CANopen FD, and device and application profiles. CAN itself is standardized by ISO in the ISO 11898 series, where CiA representatives support the work. CiA tests CANopen devices for conformance, also for non-members, and holds plugfests for CAN XL, CAN FD and CANopen devices for its members.

standards.name: CAN FD and CAN XL specifications and recommendations (CiA 6xx), CAN FD Light
standards.note: Classical CAN, CAN FD and CAN XL data link layers are standardized by ISO in ISO 11898-1.

standards.name: CANopen (CiA 3xx) and CANopen FD (CiA 13xx), with device and application profiles (CiA 4xx)
CANopen CC and CANopen FD device conformance testing
CAN XL, CAN FD and CANopen plugfests

specifications.detail: Documents with the status Public Available Specification are free to the public. Draft Specifications are for members or by yearly subscription, such as EUR 1,024 for the CAN FD and CAN XL series (CiA 6xx); work drafts are for members only.

community.detail: Company- and product-neutral CAN information is offered publicly, while partnerships, workshops and specification work are listed as member benefits.

individualFree.detail: The 2026 fee scale lists companies by size and nonprofit schools and universities; there is no individual or free tier.

organizationFree.detail: Company membership costs EUR 833 a year for 1 to 9 employees, up to EUR 11,781 above 100,000, including German VAT; half the fee when joining after 1 July.

workingGroups.detail: Membership gives access to all development stages, meeting minutes and the working groups; initiating and influencing CiA specifications is listed as a member benefit.

interopTesting.detail: CiA plugfests for CAN XL, CAN FD and CANopen devices are free of charge for members and not open to non-members.

certification.detail: CANopen CC conformance testing is open to anyone: EUR 1,000 per device session for non-members, EUR 750 for members, certificate included. It covers CANopen, not CAN itself.

openSource.detail: We found no open-source code published by CiA. The CANopen CC conformance test tool is free for members.

memberships.name: Company member
memberships.eligibility: Companies, priced by number of employees from 1 to 9 up to more than 100,000.
memberships.note: Fees include 19 % German VAT. Specifications in every status, plugfests, working groups, free CANopen vendor IDs and the CANopen CC conformance test tool.

memberships.name: School or university
memberships.eligibility: Nonprofit schools and universities.

programs.name: CANopen CC device conformance testing
programs.detail: The CiA test center checks a device's electronic data sheet, SDO and PDO handling, object dictionary, SYNC, emergency and error control and the NMT state machine, and issues a certificate: EUR 1,000 per session for non-members, EUR 750 for members.

programs.name: CiA plugfests
programs.detail: Plugfests on request for CAN XL protocol controllers and transceivers (CiA 610-1, 610-3), CAN FD controllers and transceivers, and CANopen devices and profiles. Free for members.

insights: The CAN data link itself belongs to ISO 11898, which is sold by ISO; CiA's own work sits around it, with CAN FD and CAN XL recommendations and the CANopen family. An implementer of CAN frames can work from Bosch's public CAN 2.0 and CAN FD documents and the Linux SocketCAN documentation, as go-canbus does.

CAN XL is where CiA is most active now: its plugfests test the first CAN XL controllers and transceivers. Open stacks are thin, with Linux since 6.2, can-utils, SocketCANSharp and go-canbus among the few that handle CAN XL frames.
OT Fabric is not a CiA member, implements no CiA specification yet and makes no conformance claim. CANopen is on the go-canbus roadmap, and CiA's conformance test is open to non-members.

name: OpenADR Alliance
summary: Maintains the OpenADR 2.0 and 3.0 specifications and certifies OpenADR products.
description: The OpenADR Alliance maintains the OpenADR demand response specifications and runs the certification program for OpenADR products.

specifications.detail: "The specifications are license free but copyright of the OpenADR Alliance." Downloads go through a form with terms.

community.detail: Committees, task groups and the member forums are for members.

organizationFree.detail: Contributor and Adopter memberships start at $1,500 a year.

workingGroups.detail: Committees and task groups are member benefits.

interopTesting.detail: The membership page does not mention plugfests.

certification.detail: Contributor and Sponsor members can test and certify products; Adopters cannot.

openSource.detail: Open-source OpenADR stacks exist (OpenLEADR at LF Energy, EPRI's VEN and VTN); we found none maintained by the Alliance.

memberships.name: Adopter
memberships.eligibility: Non-manufacturers: consumers, government, research agencies, test houses and regulators.
memberships.note: Votes through committees and task groups; cannot certify products.

memberships.name: Contributor
memberships.eligibility: Vendors of hardware, software or services. Under $1M revenue $1,500, $1M to $10M $3,000, $10M to $100M $5,000, over $100M $7,500.
memberships.note: Can test and certify products; IPR use for compliant products.

memberships.name: Sponsor
memberships.eligibility: Board-approved stakeholders, limited to the first nine.
memberships.note: Board seat; can lead working groups.

programs.name: OpenADR certification
programs.detail: Conformance testing and certification for Contributor and Sponsor members; test houses can apply for approved status.

related.relation: Hosts OpenLEADR, open-source OpenADR 2.0b and 3.x implementations.

name: Open Charge Alliance
summary: Develops OCPP, publishes it free, and runs certification, the OCTT test tool and plugfests.
description: The Open Charge Alliance develops the Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP) between charging stations and management systems. It publishes the specifications for free, runs a certification program with independent test labs, offers the OCPP Compliance Test Tool and organizes plugfests around the world.

specifications.detail: "OCPP is freely available for everyone to download."

community.detail: Plugfests welcome everyone in the industry; working and task groups are for members.

organizationFree.detail: Liaison membership is free, but only for standards bodies and supportive organizations that fit no other category.

workingGroups.detail: The Technical and Compliance working groups are member benefits.

interopTesting.detail: "Everyone from the EV charging industry is welcome to participate" in plugfests, held several times a year. OCTT Starter is free.

certification.detail: "Every company involved with an OCPP implementation can get an official independent OCPP Certificate"; members get discounts.

openSource.detail: Open-source OCPP stacks exist (EVerest and CitrineOS at LF Energy); we found none maintained by OCA.

memberships.name: Liaison
memberships.eligibility: Standards-setting or defining bodies (SSOs/SDOs) and supportive organizations that fit no other category. IEC experts can join as Liaison Participants.

memberships.name: Individual
memberships.eligibility: People with a professional interest in developing, distributing, installing, maintaining or using OCA standards.

memberships.name: Institutional
memberships.eligibility: Research and consulting groups, laboratories, regulators and universities.

memberships.name: Implementer
memberships.eligibility: Vendors of hardware or software implementing OCA standards. Revenue under 1M €990, 1M to 10M €2,475, 10M to 50M €4,950, over 50M €8,250.
memberships.note: OCTT Professional at the participant rate.

memberships.name: Adopter
memberships.eligibility: Organizations that deploy charging networks with OCA standards, including grid owners and operators. Same revenue bands as Implementer.

programs.name: OCPP certification
programs.detail: Run with independent test laboratories, including Dekra, DNV, the Korea Smart Grid Association, KTC and KTL.

programs.name: OCPP Compliance Test Tool (OCTT)
programs.detail: OCTT Starter is free with more than 300 core test cases. OCTT Professional is €7,900 a year for Adopter and Implementer members and €17,900 a year for others.

programs.name: OCPP Plugfest
programs.detail: Several hands-on testing events a year at partner locations worldwide.

related.relation: Hosts EVerest and CitrineOS, open-source OCPP implementations.
Works on the vehicle-to-charger side of EV charging (CCS, MCS, NACS).

insights: OCA is one of the most open organizations in this directory. The specifications are free for everyone, plugfests welcome the whole industry, certification is open to every company with an OCPP implementation, and the Starter edition of the compliance test tool is free.

Influence over the specification is a different matter: the Technical and Compliance working groups are for members. The cheapest way in is Individual membership at €297 a year; companies pay from €990 by revenue band.

The price gap that matters most for small vendors is the test tool. OCTT Professional costs €7,900 a year for Adopter and Implementer members and €17,900 for everyone else, which on its own can justify a membership.

name: CharIN
summary: Promotes the CCS, MCS and NACS charging interfaces, with working groups and Testivals.
description: CharIN is an association whose members work on the Combined Charging System (CCS), the Megawatt Charging System (MCS) and NACS for vehicle charging, with member working groups and interoperability Testivals.

standards.name: CCS, MCS and NACS charging interfaces

specifications.detail: We have not yet verified document access.

community.detail: Testivals and conferences are promoted publicly; access rules are not stated on the membership page.

organizationFree.detail: Even the startup rate is €5,000 per calendar year.

workingGroups.detail: Regular members join one or more working groups; startups get one.

interopTesting.detail: Testivals are promoted but the membership page does not say who can attend.

memberships.name: Startup
memberships.eligibility: Gross revenue under €3M, registered for less than four years, and not controlled by a Regular or Core member. Moves to the Regular rate from year three.
memberships.note: No initiation fee; access to one working group.

memberships.name: Regular
memberships.eligibility: Suppliers, utilities, public authorities, IT firms and non-profits.
memberships.note: Fees are in a dues schedule linked from the membership page, not on the page itself.

memberships.name: Core
memberships.eligibility: Founding members, and members that meet further criteria.

related.relation: OCPP covers the charger-to-back-office link; CharIN's interfaces cover the vehicle-to-charger side.

name: LF Energy
summary: Linux Foundation home for open-source energy software, including EVerest, CitrineOS, OpenLEADR and CoMPAS.
description: LF Energy is the Linux Foundation's foundation for open-source energy software, standards and data. It hosts projects such as EVerest and CitrineOS (EV charging and OCPP), OpenLEADR (OpenADR), CoMPAS (IEC 61850 tooling) and SEAPATH (digital substations), with special interest groups that anyone can join.

specifications.detail: LF Energy does not publish the protocols in this directory.

community.detail: "You can use every project, contribute to any of them, and never pay a cent."

individualFree.detail: Contributing to projects and joining SIGs needs no membership.

organizationFree.detail: Associate membership is free for eligible open-source projects, non-profits, academic institutions and government research bodies, subject to Governing Board approval.

workingGroups.detail: "SIGs are open for anyone to participate in."

interopTesting.detail: LF Energy does not run protocol test events.

certification.detail: LF Energy does not certify products.

openSource.detail: Hosts 39 projects, including EVerest, CitrineOS, openLEADR, CoMPAS and SEAPATH.

memberships.name: Contributor, no membership
memberships.eligibility: Anyone: use and contribute to every project, and join SIGs.

memberships.name: Associate
memberships.eligibility: Open-source projects, non-profits, academic institutions and government research bodies, with Governing Board approval.

memberships.name: General
memberships.eligibility: By employee count: $10,000 (up to 99) to $70,000 (5,000+) for organizations not yet in the Linux Foundation; $5,000 to $50,000 for current LF members.
memberships.note: Eligible to stand for the Governing Board.

memberships.name: Strategic
memberships.eligibility: $170,000, or $150,000 for current Linux Foundation members.
memberships.note: Seats on the Governing Board, the Technical Advisory Council and the LFESS Steering Committee.

related.relation: Publishes OCPP, which EVerest and CitrineOS implement.
Publishes OpenADR, which OpenLEADR implements.
IEC 61850 user community; CoMPAS is open-source IEC 61850 tooling.

insights: LF Energy is mostly the opposite of a protocol standards body: its projects are software, and everything it hosts is free to use and contribute to. The SIGs, including Edge Interoperability and Flexibility, are open to anyone.

Several projects on our ecosystem map live here: EVerest and CitrineOS for OCPP, and OpenLEADR for OpenADR. They are independent of the organizations that publish those protocols, which is exactly why this directory separates standards publishers from open-source foundations.

Paid membership buys governance, not access. General membership starts at $10,000 (or $5,000 for existing Linux Foundation members) and makes a company eligible for the Governing Board; Associate membership is free for open-source projects, non-profits and research bodies, with board approval.

name: Eclipse Foundation
summary: Open-source foundation behind the Sparkplug specification and Eclipse Tahu, and host of Eclipse Milo (OPC UA); committer membership is free.
description: The Eclipse Foundation is an open-source foundation. Its Sparkplug Working Group develops the Sparkplug specification, also published as ISO/IEC 20237:2023, and its projects include Eclipse Tahu, the Sparkplug reference implementation, and Eclipse Milo, an open-source OPC UA stack for Java.

standards.name: Sparkplug Compatible program and Sparkplug TCK

specifications.detail: "Anyone can implement the Sparkplug specification for any purpose without fee or royalty", under the Eclipse Foundation Specification License, with attribution.

community.detail: The membership page does not say whether non-members can contribute; we have not yet checked the contributor terms.

individualFree.detail: "There is no cost to being a Committer member", for committers whose employer is not already a member.

organizationFree.detail: Associate membership is €0 for government, research, academic and user-group organizations.

workingGroups.detail: Industry working groups have their own participation agreements; not verified yet.

interopTesting.detail: We found no Sparkplug or OPC UA interoperability event run by the foundation; the Sparkplug TCK is a conformance kit that implementers run themselves.

certification.detail: Anyone can run the Sparkplug TCK "free of charge", but "participation in the Sparkplug Compatible program is reserved for members of the Sparkplug Working Group". The foundation does not certify OPC UA products.

openSource.detail: Hosts Eclipse Tahu, the Sparkplug reference implementation, and Eclipse Milo (iot.milo).

memberships.name: Committer
memberships.eligibility: Committers on Eclipse projects whose employer is not a member.

memberships.name: Associate
memberships.eligibility: €0 for governments, research, NGOs, academia and user groups; companies pay by revenue, from €1,500 (under €1M and fewer than 10 employees) to €25,000.

memberships.name: Contributing
memberships.eligibility: €1,000 for academic and user-group organizations; companies pay by revenue, from €1,500 (under €1M and fewer than 10 employees) to €25,000.

memberships.name: Strategic
memberships.eligibility: By revenue, from €30,000 to €300,000.

programs.name: Sparkplug Compatible
programs.detail: Self-certification: a product passes the Sparkplug TCK, publishes its results summary and files a listing request, which the specification project's committers approve.

programs.name: Eclipse Sparkplug TCK
programs.detail: The Technology Compatibility Kit that checks an implementation against the specification; free to use.

related.relation: Publishes OPC UA, which Eclipse Milo implements independently.

name: International Society of Automation
summary: Publishes the ISA/IEC 62443 OT security series; standards committees are open without membership.
description: ISA is the professional society for automation. Its standards committees, including ISA99 behind the ISA/IEC 62443 industrial cybersecurity series, are open to interested parties without ISA membership.

standards.name: ISA/IEC 62443 industrial automation and control systems security (ISA99)

specifications.detail: Members get online viewing of more than 150 ISA standards; the page does not name 62443 specifically.

community.detail: Standards committee participation "shall be open to all parties who are directly and materially interested".

individualFree.detail: Committee participation needs only a free ISA account; membership itself starts at $15 for students and $170 for professionals.

workingGroups.detail: "ISA membership is not a requirement for participation in standards committees." New members usually start as non-voting information members.

interopTesting.detail: ISA does not run protocol interoperability events.

certification.detail: We have not verified product certification against 62443 yet.

memberships.name: Committee participant
memberships.eligibility: Anyone directly and materially interested, with a free ISA account.
memberships.note: New members usually join as non-voting information members.

memberships.name: Professional
memberships.eligibility: $85 in eligible countries.

related.relation: The 62443 series is published jointly as ISA/IEC 62443.
